maker: ARPA (US Department of Defense), built by BBN
summary: The US defence research network that first linked computers by packet switching. Email was invented on it, it adopted TCP/IP in 1983, and it grew into the internet before it was switched off.

image.alt: Logical map of the ARPANET in March 1977

events.note: ARPA approves funding after Bob Taylor argues for a network.

image.alt: Hand-drawn sketch of the four-node ARPANET
image.caption: The ARPANET as sketched in December 1969.

events.note: The first message goes from UCLA to SRI; the system crashes after two letters.

image.alt: Logbook entry for the first ARPANET message
image.caption: The IMP log of the first message, UCLA to SRI.

events.label: Email
events.note: Ray Tomlinson at BBN sends the first network email.

events.label: Demo
events.note: A public demonstration at a computer communications conference.

events.label: TCP/IP
events.note: Flag day: the whole network switches to TCP/IP.

events.label: MILNET
events.note: Military sites move to a separate network, MILNET.

cause: Decommissioned once the internet it gave rise to had taken over.
